# html writes its document from the first window that is always there -- one
# no `if` over state and no `for` can take away -- and shows every other window
# as a `<dialog>` in it. A program whose every window may be absent has no
# document to put a dialog in, and is refused at its first window. A window
# under an `if` over state beside an unconditional one is a dialog, and
# builds.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html cond.sngl
stderr 'cond.sngl:6:14: html writes its document from a window that is always there, and every window here is under an `if` or a `for`'

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html2 loop.sngl
stderr 'loop.sngl:6:14: html writes its document from a window that is always there, and every window here is under an `if` or a `for`'

sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html3 beside.sngl
exists html3/index.html

-- cond.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var shown = true

if shown {
    ui.window(title="Only") {
        ui.text(value="only")
    }
}
-- loop.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var names = ["a", "b"]

for var name = names {
    ui.window(title=name) {
        ui.text(value=name)
    }
}
-- beside.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var shown = true

if shown {
    ui.window(title="Maybe") {
        ui.text(value="maybe")
    }
}

ui.window(title="Always") {
    ui.text(value="always")
}
